report.reply:
I ran the problem-history scan on an up-to-date, clean `main`. There are 4 recorded problems from 2 changes, all in the app's pages. I haven't changed anything yet.

## What keeps coming back

Leave dates showing one day early happened **3 times in 2 separate changes**:
- `verifier`, leave tracker, round 2: `app/pages/leave.vue` showed dates in UTC, so a request for 3 Oct showed 2 Oct.
- `verifier`, leave calendar, round 2: `app/pages/calendar.vue` used `toISOString()`, so dates moved a day earlier in Vietnam time.
- `review`, PR #8: `app/pages/leave.vue` used `toLocaleDateString` without the app's time zone.

`CLAUDE.md` already says "Show dates with `formatDate()`", and it was still missed twice. So the lesson below makes that rule more specific. `REVIEW.md` has no date check at all. The current code no longer uses either bad pattern, so these are lessons to prevent a repeat, not fixes.

I left out the "Sumbit" typo on the Save button because it only happened once.

## Proposed lessons

1. **For building:** "Leave pages (`leave.vue`, `calendar.vue`): show every leave date with `formatDate()` from `app/utils/locale.ts`, never `toISOString()` or `toLocaleDateString()`. Twice they showed the day before in Vietnam time."
   - Evidence: verifier ×2 (leave tracker, leave calendar), review ×1 (PR #8)
2. **For review:** "Flag any `toISOString()`, `toLocaleDateString()` or `toLocaleString()` used to show a date in `app/pages/`. It must go through `formatDate()` (PR #8, verifier rounds on leave tracker and calendar)."
   - Evidence: the same 3 items

There's nothing to remove, because `LEARNED.md` has no lessons yet.

**Possible plugin issue (only a draft, not filed):** the date rule is part of the stack's defaults, and it was missed in two separate builds. I could draft an issue for `tammai/yolo-sdlc` asking the verifier to check for raw date formatting in pages. I'll only file it if you ask.

## Next step

I couldn't show you a pick-list in this session, and this step only proposes lessons. So I haven't written `LEARNED.md`, created the `learn/2026-09-28` branch or committed. If you approve (both lessons is my recommendation), I'll add them under the right headings, commit "Learn: 2 lessons" and ship it with `/yolo-sdlc:ship`. It will be a red change because `LEARNED.md` is engineer-owned, so it gets the engineer review.

Several connected services (Asana, Linear, Slack, GitHub and others) aren't signed in. This task didn't need any of them, but they won't work until you connect them in claude.ai connector settings or with `/mcp`.

report.reply:
This covers the app's last 3 merged changes.

| Stage | What it measures | Value | Based on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Plan | Time from idea to agreed examples (typical) | 20 min | 3 changes |
| 2 Design | Examples reworked after the build started | 33% | 3 changes |
| 3 Build | Passed verification on the first try | 67% | 3 changes |
| 3 Build | Time from plan to built (typical) | 50 min | 3 changes |
| 4 Test | Passed the automatic checks on the first run | 67% | 3 changes |
| 5 Deploy | Time from pull request to merged (typical) | 30 min | 3 changes |
| 5 Deploy | Engineer reviews that raised warnings | 50% | 2 reviews |
| 5 Deploy | Warnings shipped without a fix | 2 | 2 reviews |
| 5 Deploy | Releases per week | 3.0 | 3 changes |
| 6 Maintain | Changes that came from a user's problem report | 0% | 3 changes |

**What it means:**

- **Nothing came from user problem reports (0%).** Every change started as someone's own idea, so what people hit in the live app isn't feeding back yet. **The one thing to try:** have an engineer run `/yolo-sdlc:triage` to turn reports from the "Report a problem" button into new ideas.
- **2 engineer-review warnings went live without a fix.** That's not a problem in itself, but an engineer should look at them to confirm neither one matters.
- **1 of 3 changes needed its examples reworked after building began**, and 1 of 3 failed verification or the automatic checks on the first try. With so few changes, these could be one-offs.
- **Work moves quickly.** It takes about 20 minutes to agree the examples and about 30 minutes to merge once the pull request is open.

**What the numbers can't show:** each figure rests on only 2 or 3 changes, so one change swings a figure by 33 percentage points. Treat them as early signals, not trends. Any work done before these skills were in use has no stage times and isn't reflected here. The picture gets more reliable after about 10 changes.

The report only read existing records. Nothing in the app, its pull requests or its labels was changed.
